subject.title: [Feature]: Self-evolving SOUL.md via opt-in reflection sub-turn + soul_update tool

question: Should OpenClaw core accept model-mediated, opt-in writes to SOUL.md, or should durable preference capture stay in memory/plugin surfaces until a narrower core API is designed?
rationale: This changes durable prompt-loaded instruction state and adds config, tool, CLI, and notification semantics; automation cannot choose that security/product boundary.

options.title: Accept core SOUL auto-update after hardening
options.body: Sponsor the linked PR direction but require private tool capability, send-policy ordering, channel-visible notices or local-only scope, and focused security tests before merge.

options.title: Move preference capture to memory/plugin work
options.body: Keep SOUL.md manual and use memory/plugin surfaces for durable preferences unless a missing extension API is identified.

options.title: Pause until a broader persona persistence design
options.body: Leave this issue open as product design until maintainers settle SOUL.md, MEMORY.md, audit, and undo semantics together.

recommendation.title: Accept core SOUL auto-update after hardening
recommendation.body: Sponsor the linked PR direction but require private tool capability, send-policy ordering, channel-visible notices or local-only scope, and focused security tests before merge.

likelyOwner.reason: The history links this area to SOUL docs/templates and broader agent/workspace architecture decisions.
